questions.question_text: In a 100 m race, Atul finishes first. He is ahead of Bala by 10 m and ahead of Chirag by 19 m. In another race of the same distance, Bala defeats Dheeraj by 23.5 m. By what distance does Chirag defeat Dheeraj in the 100 m race?
questions.solution_text:
We know that $Time=\dfrac{Dist}{Speed}$
Let Atul's speed be A, Bala's speed be B, Chirag's speed be C and Dheeraj's speed be D. 
Atul beats Bala by 10m. This means that by the time Atul covers 100m, Bala only covers 90. Therefore - 
-> $\dfrac{100}{A}=\dfrac{90}{B}\rightarrow1$
Atul beats Chirag by 19m. This means that by the time Atul covers 100m, Chirag only covers 81m. Therefore - 
-> $\dfrac{100}{A}=\dfrac{81}{C}\rightarrow2$
Equating eq. 1 and eq. 2 -
$\dfrac{90}{B}=\dfrac{81}{C}$
$\dfrac{90}{B}\times\dfrac{100}{90}=\dfrac{81}{C}\times\dfrac{100}{90}$
$\dfrac{100}{B}=\dfrac{90}{C}\rightarrow3$
Bala beats Dheeraj by 23.5m. This means that by the time Bala covers 100m, Dheeraj only covers 76.5m. Therefore -
-> $\dfrac{100}{B}=\dfrac{76.5}{D}\rightarrow4$
Equating eq. 3 and eq. 4 -
$\dfrac{90}{C}=\dfrac{76.5}{D}$
$\dfrac{90}{C}\times\dfrac{100}{90}=\dfrac{76.5}{D}\times\dfrac{100}{90}$
$\dfrac{100}{C}=\dfrac{85}{D}$
This means that by the time Chirag covers 100m, Dheeraj covers only 85m. Therefore, Chirag beat Dheeraj by 15m.

questions.question_text: In a trapezium ABCD, AB=23 and CD=5. The lengths of the diagonals are AC=25 and BD=17. Find the length of side CB.
questions.solution_text:
Using the given figure, let us extend AB to a point E such that DB is parallel to CE. 
We can then find the area of the triangle AEC from Heron's Formula. 
Using Heron's formula, which is $\triangle=\sqrt{s\left(s-a\right)\left(s-b\right)\left(s-c\right)}$
Where $s$ is the semi-perimeter, $s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}$
AE will be 23+5=28, AC will equal 25, and CE will equal DB, which is 17. 
$\triangle=\sqrt{\left(35\right)\left(7\right)\left(10\right)\left(18\right)}=210$
We can drop a perpendicular CF, and then we have, 
Using this, we get, 
$210=\frac{1}{2}\left(AE\right)\left(CF\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(28\right)\left(CF\right)$
$CF=15$
From Pythagoras' theorem in triangle AFC, we obtain, 
$AF=\sqrt{AC^2-CF^2}=\sqrt{625-225}=20$
FB=AB-AF
FB=23-20=3. 
Using Pythagoras' theorem for FBC, we get, 
$CB=\sqrt{CF^2+FB^2}=\sqrt{225+9}=\sqrt{234}=3\sqrt{26}$
Hence, the answer is $3\sqrt{26}$

Then MNCD is a rectangle [as AB||DC , so considering DM as transveral $\angle\ DMN=\angle MDC=\ 90^{\circ\ }\ \ $ ; similarly for the other pair of angles ].  So, we will have DC=MN =5 units. Further, let BN= a units. Then we get $AM=AB-MN-BN=\ 23-5-a=18-a$ .
The figure is updated accordingly.

or, $DM^2+\ \left(5+a\right)^2=17^2$
or, $DM^2=17^2-\ \left(5+a\right)^2$ _______(1)
Again, considering $\triangle\ ACN$, $CN^2+\ AN^2=AC^2$
or, $CN^2+\ \left(5+18-a\right)^2=25^2$
or, $CN^2=25^2-\left(23-a\right)^2$ ________(2)
Now, both DM and CN are altitudes for the same trapezium, and so they have to be equal; hence, comparing (1) and (2),
$25^2-\left(23-a\right)^2=17^2-\left(5+a\right)^2$
or, $25^2-17^2=\left(23-a\right)^2-\left(5+a\right)^2$

Now, $CB=DM=\sqrt{\ 17^2-\left(5+3\right)^2}=15$ units
Finally, in right triangle CBN, 
$BN^2+CN^2=CB^2$

Ravi is planning to buy rice in bulk. The grocery store offers him two types of discounts: 

A) He receives a 10% discount on his entire purchase, or 

B) He gets 1 kg of rice free for every 10 kg of rice he buys. 

Ravi needs 100 kg of rice. Which deal is better?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Deal A is better than Deal B by $1\ \dfrac{9}{91}\ \%\ $

options.label: B
options.option_text: Deal B is better than Deal A by $1\ \dfrac{9}{91}\ \%\ $

options.label: C
options.option_text: Deal A is better than Deal B by $1\ \dfrac{1}{9}\ \%\ $

questions.solution_text:
Let Ravi pay Rs. x for 1 kg of rice, ie the price in which the shop keeper sells rice is Rs x.
For Deal A, he gets a discount of 10% on the price. Total amount Ravi will have to pay is $90\ \%\ \ of\ 100x=90x$
For Deal B, he gets 1 kg of rice free for every 10 kg of rice purchased. 
So he gets 9 kg of rice free for 90 kgs of rice purchased , ie in total he gets 99 kg but pays for only 90. The remaining 1 kg rice that is required will have no discount. so in total he will have to pay for 90+1=91 kg of rice, which will cost him  Rs.91x 
Clearly deal A is better than Deal B.
Deal A is better than Deal B by $\dfrac{Amount_{Deal\ B}-Amount_{Deal\ A}}{Amount_{Deal\ B}}\times\ 100\%=\dfrac{91x-90x}{91x}\times\ 100=\dfrac{100}{91}\ \%\ =1\ \dfrac{9}{91}\ \%\ $

(Take: $\pi\ =\dfrac{22}{7}$)

And the total area of grass field  $=lb\ =12\times8=96\ m^2$

                                            =  $\dfrac{\ 25\left(22\right)}{7\times4\times96}$
                                           =  $0.2046$
                                           =  $20.46\%$

If $\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]+\left\{z\right\}=9.4$

$\left[x\right]+\left\{y\right\}+\left[z\right]=11.8$

$\left\{x\right\}+\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]=10.1$

Then find the value of $\left[x-y+z\right]$

(where, $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$ and $\left\{x\right\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$)
questions.solution_text:
Given,
$\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$ and $\left\{x\right\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$
So from the equation, 
$\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]+\left\{z\right\}=9.4$
we can say, $\left\{z\right\}=0.4$ and $\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]=9$ ------>(1)
(as decimal part will only be in $\left\{z\right\}$ and $\left[x\right]$ and $\left[y\right]$ will have integral values).
Similarly, $\left[x\right]+\left\{y\right\}+\left[z\right]=11.8$
or, $\left\{y\right\}=0.8$ and  $\left[x\right]+\left[z\right]=11$ ------->(2)
Also, $\left\{x\right\}+\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]=10.1$
or, $\left\{x\right\}=0.1$ and $\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]=10$ -------->(3)
Now adding equation (1),(2) and (3),
$\left(\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]\right)+\left(\left[x\right]+\left[z\right]\right)+\left(\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]\right)=9+11+10$
or, $2\left(\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]\right)=30$
so, $\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]+\left[z\right]=15$
Now from equation (1), since $\left[x\right]+\left[y\right]=9$, so $\left[z\right]=15-9=6$
Similarly we can find $\left[y\right]=4$ and $\left[x\right]=5$
Now, $x=\left[x\right]+\left\{x\right\}=5+0.1=5.1$
$y=\left[y\right]+\left\{y\right\}=4+0.8=4.8$
$z=\left[z\right]+\left\{z\right\}=6+0.4=6.4$
So, $x-y+z=5.1-4.8+6.4=6.7$
So, $\left[x-y+z\right]=6$

$\frac{240}{5x+3x}=\frac{240}{8x}=10$
$\Rightarrow x = 3$
Hari's speed is 9m/s. Because Hari is travelling opposite to the stream, his relative speed will be 9-6 = 3 m/s
The total time taken by Hari will be $\frac{240}{3}=80$

We are told that the ratio of these two is 9:10

From this we get z = 4.
The ratio of A and C is 6k:4k = 3:2
The value of a+b = 5

questions.question_text: If a, b are distinct integers and $f(x)=x^2+ax+b$ , $g(x)=x^2+bx+a$ , and the differences between the roots of $f(x)=0$ & $g(x)=0$ are equal . Then which of the following holds true ?
questions.solution_text:
Let $\left(\alpha,\ \beta\right)\ \ $ be the roots of $f(x)=0$ and $(h,k)$ be the roots of $g(x)=0$.
For $f(x)=0$ : 
$x^2+ax+b=0$
$\alpha+\beta\ =-a$ 
$\alpha\beta\ =b\ $     
                $\left(\alpha-\beta\ \right)^2=\left(\alpha+\beta\right)^2-4\alpha\ \beta\ $
                                           $=a^2-4b$     
For $g(x)=0$ : 
$x^2+bx+a=0$
$h+k\ =-b$
$hk=a$
            $(h-k)^2=\left(h+k\right)^2-4hk$
                              $=b^2-4a$
As the difference of roots of both the quadratic equations are equal, the squares of difference of roots must also be equal. 
               $b^2-4a=a^2-4b$
             $a^2-b^2=4\left(b-a\right)$
             $\left(a+b\right)\left(a-b\right)=4\left(b-a\right)$
As, it is mentioned that a & b are distinct integers , we can say $a-b\ne\ 0$.
                 Hence,  $a+b+4=0$
Therefore, Option D .

questions.question_text: Ajay takes a loan of Rs. 12,300 at 13% simple interest for two years. At the same time, Jatin takes the same loan amount at 10% compound interest for two years. He paid the amount in two instalments; the second was thrice the first. What is the difference between the interest (in rupees) paid by Ajay and Jatin?
questions.solution_text:
We know Simple interest formula is $\ \dfrac{\ P\times\ R\times\ T}{100}$
Now, Ajay takes a loan of Rs 12300 at 13% simple interest for two years. 
$P=12300,\ R=13,\ T=2$
Interest paid by Ajay = $\ \dfrac{\ P\times\ R\times\ T}{100}$ = $\ \dfrac{\ 12300\times\ 13\times\ 2}{100}$ = $3198$ rupees
Now, Jatin takes the same loan amount at 10% compound interest for two years. So, the total amount to be paid at the end of two years is -
$=P\left(1+\ \dfrac{\ R}{100}\right)^{T\ }=12300\left(1+\ \dfrac{\ 10}{100}\right)^2=14883$ rupees
But he paid the amount in two installments, and the second was thrice the first. Let us assume the first installment is I, and the second will be 3I.
This means - $3\times\ I\ +\ 1.1\times\ I\ =14883$ rupees
  $=>I=3630$ rupees
So total amount paid by Jatin at the end of two years = $\ I\ +\ 3I$ $=4I=14520$ rupees
So, total interest paid by Jatin $=14520-12300\ =\ 2220$ rupees
Therefore, the difference between the amount paid by Ajay and Jatin $=3198-2220=978$ rupees.

questions.question_text: A circle, with a radius of 5 units is centred at O. It has 2 parallel chords AB and PQ on the same side of the centre, separated by a distance of 1 unit. The length of chord AB is 6 units, find the area of the quadrilateral ABPQ in $unit^2$.

Since both the chords are on the same side of the centre, we can draw the figure as follows:
We know that the radius = 5, Therefore OB = OQ = 5
Also, we know that AB = 6
Therefore, AM = MB = $\frac{6}{2}=3$
Therefore, we can find OM using Pythagoras theorem,
OM = $\sqrt{\ 5^2-3^2}=\sqrt{\ 25-9}=4$
It is given that the distance between the chords is 1, so MN= 1
Hence, ON = OM - MN = 4 - 1 = 3
NQ = $\sqrt{\ OQ^2-ON^2}=\sqrt{\ 5^2-3^2}=\sqrt{\ 25-6}=4$
Hence, PQ = $2\times\ 4=8$
The quadrilateral ABPQ is a trapezium. Hence, area = $\frac{1}{2}\times\ \left(6+8\right)\times\ 1$ = 7
